business_problem: When the pandemic disrupted the medical supply chain and forced millions of patients to postpone their elective surgeries, the company realized it needed a better global view of supply and demand. The COVID-19 pandemic only intensified the company’s challenges.
solution_summary: Integra Life Sciences provides the products physicians and clinicians need to perform surgeries around the globe. When the pandemic disrupted the medical supply chain and forced millions of patients to postpone their elective surgeries, the company realized it needed a better global view of supply and demand. Integra replaced its aging data warehouse with Azure Databricks and achieved immediate reductions in data processing times, data availability lag, data warehouse loading time and other key metrics. The company now moves its products with confidence, knowing that it is doing its part to enhance the quality of care for millions of people worldwide. Seeking to regain visibility into its inventory and drive growth during challenging times, Integra launched a strategic transformation. The company had been processing data on IBM DataStage, which took long hours to run and offered little flexibility.

solution_components.name: Azure Databricks
solution_components.role: Provides the Azure-based lakehouse workspace for ingesting, transforming, and serving governed data.

solution_components.name: Databricks Data + AI Platform
solution_components.role: Provides the shared lakehouse environment for ingestion, engineering, analytics, and AI workloads.

data_flow: Customer, product, and engagement data lands in Azure Databricks, is transformed in the lakehouse.
business_outcome: Reported outcomes include 69% Reduction in data processing time; 52% Reduction in data availability lag; 45% Reduction in overall operating costs.
metrics: Azure Databricks architecture supports 500 data objects, 700 data pipelines
